chunks.title: JavaScript Ternary Operator
chunks.text: The ternary operator is a conditional operator.

chunks.title: JavaScript Ternary Operator
chunks.text: It's basically a shorthand if statement.

chunks.title: JavaScript Ternary Operator
chunks.text: It tests a condition, then returns a value if true, or another value if false.

chunks.title: JavaScript Ternary Operator
chunks.text: Here's an example of an if statement.

chunks.title: JavaScript Ternary Operator
chunks.text: We are generating a random number between 1 and 10.

chunks.title: JavaScript Ternary Operator
chunks.text: Then we are checking to see if the number is divisible by 2, and if the remainder is

chunks.title: JavaScript Ternary Operator
chunks.text: If it is, then the number would be even, if not, it's odd.

chunks.title: JavaScript Ternary Operator
chunks.text: We can turn this into a ternary operator by removing the if-else statement.

chunks.title: JavaScript Ternary Operator
chunks.text: We start with the condition, then we have a question mark.

chunks.title: JavaScript Ternary Operator
chunks.text: The statement after the question mark is what will happen if the condition is true.

chunks.title: JavaScript Ternary Operator
chunks.text: After that we have a colon, and the statement after the colon is what will happen if the

chunks.title: JavaScript Ternary Operator
chunks.text: condition is false.

chunks.title: JavaScript Ternary Operator
chunks.text: We can also rewrite this by moving the redundant message equals to the beginning.

chunks.title: JavaScript Ternary Operator
chunks.text: But what if we want to perform multiple operations if the condition is true or false?

chunks.title: JavaScript Ternary Operator
chunks.text: It's pretty straightforward in the if statement.

chunks.title: JavaScript Ternary Operator
chunks.text: In the ternary operator, we can do the same thing by wrapping each set of operations in

chunks.title: JavaScript Ternary Operator
chunks.text: parentheses and separating each operation with a comma.

chunks.title: JavaScript Ternary Operator
chunks.text: Here's one last example that's a bit more real world.

chunks.title: JavaScript Ternary Operator
chunks.text: Here we have a subscribe checkbox, and we're listening for the change event.

chunks.title: JavaScript Ternary Operator
chunks.text: On the change, we will set the message dependent on whether the checkbox is checked or not.
